title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from 2.1, begun on the previous page). X and Y are smooth projective varieties, with n = dim X and m = dim Y. B_X = Pic^0_red(X) is the Picard variety of X and A_Y = Alb(Y) is the Albanese variety of Y. z is a cycle class on X×Y of codimension n+m-1, so that for a divisor d on X, z(d) = pr_{Y*}(z·(d×Y)) is a 0-cycle on Y. S_Y : Cyc_0^0(Y) → A_Y is the Albanese summation map. The goal is a homomorphism u = u_z : B_X → A_Y with S_Y(z(d)) = u(cl(d)) for every divisor d algebraically equivalent to 0.

Previous page. Let Θ ∈ A^1(X×B_X) be the Poincaré class, normalised so that Θ(o) = 0. Set C = π_*((1_Y×Θ)·(z×1_{B_X})) ∈ Z^m(Y×B_X). This is a family of 0-cycles on Y parametrised by B_X, i.e. the composite correspondence z∘Θ. Since z(Θ(o)) = 0, applying 1.1 (a family of 0-cycles on Y over a base T induces a homomorphism A_T → A_Y) gives u : B_X = A_{B_X} → A_Y with S_Y(z(Θ(b))) = u(b).

This page.
(1) The construction is compatible with cohomology: the map u induces on H^1 the map that cl(z) induces from H^1(X) to H^{2m-1}(Y)(m). Grothendieck says this follows from 1.6 by redoing the construction cohomologically.
(2) u depends linearly (additively) on z.
(3) If z is numerically equivalent to 0, then so is C, being a composite of correspondences (projection formula). By 1.1, u is then 0. So u_z depends only on the numerical class of z. Implicitly this uses that a homomorphism of abelian varieties induced by a numerically trivial family is zero, which follows from Weil's positivity of the Rosati trace form.
(4) Variant of the proof. Use Hom(B_X, A_Y) = Hom(B_X, B_Y^*), where A_Y is dual to B_Y. By Weil, this group is the group of divisorial correspondence classes on B_X×B_Y. Take the Poincaré classes Θ_X on X×B_X and Θ_Y on Y×B_Y and form the composite correspondence Θ_Y ∘ Z ∘ ᵗΘ_X, a codimension-one class on B_X×B_Y. The codimension check is 1 + (n+m-1) + 1 - n - m = 1. This gives u_Z directly as a divisorial correspondence.

The advantage of the variant shows on the next page. Corollary 2.2, ᵗ(u_Z) = u(ᵗZ), becomes essentially formal: transposing Z transposes the divisor class on B_X×B_Y. The crossed-out start of Corollary 2.2 on this page ('every homomorphism B_X → A_Y is defined by a Z_1 ∈ Cyc(X×Y)') is a surjectivity statement that Grothendieck abandoned here.
errors: The deduction 'C num. equiv. to 0 ⇒ u = 0, by virtue of 1.1' is only valid if 1.1 includes the statement that numerically trivial families of 0-cycles induce the zero homomorphism. That needs Weil's positivity (Rosati trace form) or a cohomological argument via homological equivalence. As written it is a pointer, not a proof.
The notation switches between z (on this page and the previous one) and Z (in the variant) for the same correspondence.

The cohomological compatibility is only asserted ('se déduit par exemple de 1.6'), not verified. The next page itself warns 'attention aux signes éventuels', so signs in the transposition and duality identifications are not controlled.

The crossed-out surjectivity statement (every homomorphism B_X → A_Y comes from a cycle) was abandoned. In general it is only known for divisor-type cases, or conditionally under Lefschetz-type hypotheses (cf. the next page's 2.4).

ideas.what: Homomorphism Pic^0(X) → Alb(Y) induced by a correspondence of codimension dim X + dim Y - 1, via the Poincaré family and the universal property of the Albanese
ideas.modern_name: Action of correspondences on Picard/Albanese varieties; the H^1-part of motives (Murre's Picard and Albanese motives)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Grothendieck's motive programme as reported by Demazure, Kleiman and Manin; not in EGA/SGA explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: u_z depends only on the numerical class of z
ideas.modern_name: Correspondences acting on abelian varieties factor through numerical equivalence (via Weil positivity)
ideas.where_published: Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (in Dix exposés), which reflects Grothendieck's ideas

ideas.what: Variant: Hom(B_X, A_Y) = Hom(B_X, B_Y^*) = divisorial correspondences on B_X×B_Y, with u_Z = Θ_Y ∘ Z ∘ ᵗΘ_X
ideas.modern_name: Weil's identification Hom(A, B^∨) = DivCorr(A, B); composition with Poincaré correspondences

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard working-out of Weil-style correspondence theory between Picard and Albanese varieties, with the transposition symmetry made formal. It is well covered by Weil, Lieberman, Kleiman and Murre. There is no new construction, and the one non-routine claim (surjectivity onto Hom) was crossed out.
transcription_corrections: The superscript in 'Z ∈ A^{n-m}(X×Y)' is very likely 'A^{n+m-1}(X×Y)'. Only that codimension makes Θ_Y∘Z∘ᵗΘ_X a divisor class and makes z(d) a 0-cycle; the handwriting shows 'n', then something, then a trailing dash.
Line 6: 'ça dépend linéairement de z, et si z est num. équiv. à 0, il en est de même de C, donc de u en vertu de 1.1' — the reading 'linéairement' is correct.
The crossed-out lines at the bottom read: 'Corollaire 2.2. Tout homomorphisme B_X → A_Y est défini par un Z_1 ∈ Cycl(X×Y).' The machine reading 'Thm homomorphismes' should be 'Tout homomorphisme'.
